title: Left exact sheafification for Grothendieck abelian coefficients
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal V$. Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a $\mathcal V$-small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category relative to $\mathcal V$, with $\mathcal V$-small morphism sets [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let $\operatorname{PSh}(\mathcal C;\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ and let $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$ be its full subcategory of sheaves: for each $T\in\mathcal A$, the presheaf of sets $U\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(T,F(U))$ is a sheaf. The inclusion $\iota$ admits a left adjoint $a$ (sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]), and $a$ preserves finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]. The category $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$ is abelian.

proof.text: Choose a generator $G$ of $\mathcal A$ using [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. By [lem-coef-grothendieck-locally-presentable], $\mathcal A$ is locally presentable; applying [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] to $G$ gives an infinite regular $\kappa_0\in\mathcal V$ for which $\operatorname{Hom}(G,-)$ preserves $\kappa_0$-filtered colimits. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the two $\mathcal V$-small sets $\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal C)$ and the initial ordinal of $\kappa_0$. Obtain an infinite regular $\kappa$ strictly larger than both cardinalities. A $\kappa$-filtered category is $\kappa_0$-filtered directly from the definition, so $G$ is also $\kappa$-presentable. Thus the generator, presentability and site-size hypotheses of the transfinite construction all hold in the original universe.

proof.text: For each presheaf $P$, take the functorial plus iteration $Q_\kappa(P)$ specified in [lem-sfb-transfinite-plus-sheaf-convergence]: start at $P$, apply the matching-family plus construction at successors and take colimits at limits and at $\kappa$. This is a real construction, not an object chosen from an existence assertion. By that node, with the $G$ and $\kappa$ of step 1, its value satisfies exactly the Hom-tested sheaf condition in this item. Corestrict its functor on presheaves to the full subcategory of sheaves and call the resulting functor $a$. On natural transformations it is the same plus iteration; identities and compositions hold because corestriction to a full subcategory does not alter morphisms.

proof.text: The canonical $\eta_P:P\to Q_\kappa(P)=\iota a(P)$ of this construction induces, by [lem-sfb-transfinite-plus-sheaf-orthogonality], natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{PSh}}(\iota a(P),\iota F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{PSh}}(P,\iota F)$ for all sheaves $F$. Since sheaves form a full subcategory, the left side is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}}(a(P),F)$. These natural bijections are the adjunction $a\dashv\iota$, and assert precisely the universal property of sheafification in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The orthogonality lemma imposes no unproved sheafification-existence assumption.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-transfinite-plus-finite-limits] to the same site, coefficient category, generator and regular cardinal chosen in step 1. Its corestricted functor is the functor $a$ just constructed in step 2, so it preserves finite limits. This is preservation for the actual sheaf-valued functor, not merely for an endofunctor on presheaves; no separate identification of two independently chosen reflectors is required.

proof.text: The coefficient category $\mathcal A$ is abelian by [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Steps 3 and 4 give a left adjoint to the sheaf inclusion and its finite-limit preservation. Therefore [lem-sfb-abelian-sheaves-left-exact-reflector], applied with $\mathcal B=\mathcal A$ and $L=a$, gives that $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$ is abelian. Its sheaf condition is the same Hom-tested condition used in step 2, so this concludes every clause of the item.
